historical_reviews.deepseek: Correctly identifies a security-state write and approval need, but its literal credentials and incomplete verification would create persistent predictable access.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Correctly expands the case into a controlled account lifecycle across all three source interfaces.
historical_reviews.history: No earlier exact source identity record exists.
historical_reviews.v3_1: Creation success must prove both positive access at the approved role and negative privilege boundaries. Authentication alone cannot show RoleId was enforced; cleanup must also invalidate active sessions/tokens, not merely remove the collection member.

original_test_intent: Verify that one uniquely named temporary BMC user can be created with an approved role, authenticate through IPMI, Redfish and BMC-Web with correct privilege enforcement, and be fully removed or disabled without affecting existing accounts.
original_method: Inventory existing accounts, generate a unique vault-held identity, validate password and role mappings, obtain approval, POST one least-privilege account through protected Redfish, read it back, test permitted authentication and bounded privilege behavior across IPMI/Redfish/Web, then disable/delete it, invalidate sessions and compare final inventory to baseline.
manual_activity: The BMC security owner approves the generated identity, role and lifecycle, verifies the BMC-Web login/privilege experience, observes cleanup and confirms no existing or recovery account was altered.
required_inputs: Approved positive and negative privilege matrix
safety_requirements: Never expose secrets in URLs, history, logs or screenshots
Do not use unapproved TLS bypass
Keep an independent recovery administrator active
Do not treat authentication as privilege proof
Stop on collision, overprivilege or cleanup ambiguity
agent_execution_scope: Verify target, schema, password and role policy
Create and read back one account
Test IPMI, Redfish and Web authentication plus bounded privileges
Compare final inventory and archive redacted evidence
engineer_actions: Approve identity lifecycle and least-privilege role
Confirm Web behavior and privilege boundaries

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The collection POST fits account creation, but fixed credentials, `-k`, absent collision checks and no IPMI/Redfish/Web privilege or cleanup proof fail the source lifecycle.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: After inventory and approval, POST one vendor-valid AccountService object using a vault-generated unique credential and least-privilege RoleId over protected TLS; verify object, multi-interface authentication and role boundaries, then disable/delete and revoke sessions.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The new-user creation and IPMI/Redfish/BMC-Web checks remain; the 5/5-minute estimate is retained as source metadata but secure lifecycle and cleanup may require a longer governed window.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use one audit identifier to link pre-inventory, approved role matrix, redacted create/readback, protocol/web session results, negative privilege probes, cleanup, session invalidation and final inventory.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Replaces literal shared passwords and login-only checks with vault-backed identity uniqueness, authorization boundaries and complete revocation.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Successful logins cannot prove the correct account object, role enforcement, absence of credential leakage or removal of residual sessions.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: BMC role vocabularies and IPMI privilege levels may not map one-to-one; only vendor-approved equivalence and safe read-only negative checks may be used.

project_override_considerations: The source wording says adjust password, but the collection POST, new username and three new-account login steps consistently implement account creation with an initial password; treat the wording as a label defect, not authorization to modify an existing user. Project policy must define the exact temporary role and cleanup timing.
expected_evidence: Target/AccountService identity, password/role policy and redacted baseline inventory
Owner approval and unique vault identity reference without secret value
Redacted POST and exact account GET with role/enabled state
IPMI, Redfish and BMC-Web authentication plus allowed/denied privilege results
Disable/delete, session invalidation, final inventory equality and recovery-admin proof
Secret-leak scan, preserved audit logs and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, collection POST, new username and multi-interface login steps consistently define new-account creation; 'Adjust account password' wording describes setting the initial password and does not create a separate existing-account objective.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Schema, role mapping, vault identity, browser verification and cleanup are identifiable package/operator inputs. Execution becomes BLOCKED if least privilege or complete account/session cleanup cannot be guaranteed.

review_improvement: Turns predictable credential creation into an auditable least-privilege lifecycle that tests all source interfaces and leaves no persistent management access.
independent_technical_reasoning: A management account is both an object and a set of authorization/session effects. The review must prove uniqueness, correct role, usable intended protocols, denied excess privileges and complete revocation. Omitting any dimension can leave a formally created yet overprivileged or persistent access path even when all login attempts succeed.
